title: TikTok is Risen!
subtitle: A miracle has occurred, of the most limited nature.
body_html:
Readers, harken to me! Gather round! A miracle has occurred. No, it not the second coming of Jesus. That would be a bit much. It's not the rapture. It’s not aliens—they are here already, as we have covered. It’s TikTok. No sooner had I written a eulogy for its demise, but The D*nald, in some early morning Sunday magic, resurrected the app!

He's gonna do something, that's gonna have some dubious legal basis, but who cares. Everybody can now understand what's trending and viral beverage fridges, and makeup, and Temu partnerships, and we can all rejoice.

There will be videos celebrating.

But for one brief and beautiful moment, we had poetry, and not endless videos. Now, if you’ll excuse me, I’ve gotta go learn something about what it's like to work at a “spicy ranch,” from an HR perspective, presumable because the algorithm has figured out I love HR themed content, or… perhaps which thinly veiled cannabis product is now available to me, or how I can order seafood that comes over the Internet based on the recommendation of a seafood themed creator, or which torture techniques were popular in the 1800s, or which mathematical equations best describe the movement of the planets around the sun, or what's happening in South Korea, or which ax is the best for splitting wood, assuming it's swung by someone who is very masculine in appearance, or what Austin Nasso thinks Donald Trump would say—as hilarious parody—about whatever is happening right now, or so many other issues without which we would have 15 seconds of content less than we now have endless and unfettered access to. These options and more are what TikTok hath brought me, which will be different from what it brings you, thus the power of the For You feed.

Honestly, this may go down in the annals of the most pointless lawmaking, and law undoing, that I can possibly imagine. If Congress can make a law, and the Supreme Court can uphold it, and the president can just unilaterally dismiss its impact? We have got a real problem. We've got a lack of what, in early childhood development, we call object permanence. But, for laws.

One of the problems with fickle leaders is, of course, that we don't know what is true, over a time scale any longer than the whims of the leader. There have been other notable fickle leaders, throughout history. We tend to remember them with a lack of fondness.

But, seriously, TikTok works again. Thank goodness, right?

If you will excuse me, I need to go make some videos about UnitedHealth Group that will be a Hit in the Philippines.
